why: A is 27 theorems (universes at 0): transport existence/uniqueness at the polyfold level (exists_unique_transport_of_isLR, ..._of_isLRLocal, ..._of_isEffective, ..._polyfold, transport, transport_left), the SEP-level Theorem 12.5.7 (2) (theorem_12_5_7_two_orbitMap_unique_of_isLR/LRLocal), diagram lemmas and half-space / ℤ/3 examples. The two statements differ in hypotheses: every transport statement of A assumes that the model of the given orientation is tame, admits sc-smooth bump functions and carries a tame sc-Fredholm section; B's existence (1) and uniqueness (2) assume none of this, and the project has no route to either without them, so A ⇒ B stops there. The conclusions also differ in form: A's o' is a family characterised by the pull-back equations over every diagram of every admissible 𝔄 (Γ-compatible, pushing F to F'), and A concludes that b's model has sc⁺-sections through every point, which B (1) assumes; B's transport is a Correspondence (one diagram with Φ^*o = Ψ^*o'), and B (2) only compares orientations reached through some correspondence. So B gives neither the SEP-level statements, nor the diagram-independence, nor the sc⁺-section conclusion, nor the examples, and B ⇒ A stops. B's clause (0) is the definition of IsOrientable (B_clause0_holds, Iff.rfl). Main conjunct alone: same diagnosis.
B_issue: The text's Definition 16.6.5 is stated for a tame strong polyfold bundle, and Theorem 12.5.7, which it invokes, for strong bundles over tame ep-groupoids. B quantifies over every strong polyfold bundle with no tameness assumption (and no sc-smooth bump functions, which the project carries as Part I's standing hypothesis), so B (1) and (2) claim the transport in a setting the text does not cover.
